title: Count of Interesting Subarrays
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<long long,long long> mp: up to n+1 entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned long long
approach: Define `cnt[i]` = number of indices `j < i` with `nums[j] % modulo == k`. A subarray `[l, r]` is interesting iff `(cnt[r+1] - cnt[l]) % modulo == k`, i.e. `cnt[l] % modulo == (cnt[r+1] - k + modulo) % modulo`. Sweep `i` from `0` to `n`, maintaining a hash map of how many earlier prefix counts have each residue; for each `i`, add `map[(cnt[i] - k + modulo) % modulo]` to the answer, then increment `map[cnt[i] % modulo]`.
hints: For a subarray from l to r, the count of "special" indices depends only on two prefix-level counts. With n up to 10^5, checking all O(n^2) subarrays is too slow - what single piece of information per position would let you count matching subarrays ending there in constant time?

Use a hash map keyed by prefix-count residue (mod modulo). In Example 1 (modulo=2, k=1), after processing index 0 the prefix count is 1; you look up residue `(1 + 2 − 1) % 2 = 0` in the map, find 1 match, then store residue `1 % 2 = 1`.

```
map = {0: 1}
count = 0
answer = 0
for each x in nums:
    if x % modulo == k: count++
    target = (count % modulo + modulo - k) % modulo
    answer += map[target]
    map[count % modulo]++
return answer
```
